category_title: Young immigrant boys labeled as 'struggling readers' who exhibit non-normative behavioral engagement (e.g., movement, talk, and gaze aversion) during literacy tasks
scenario_title: Independent writing activity with rigid product expectations
minimal_context: The student is sitting at a table with peers during a writing workshop, tasked with completing an independent writing activity about what his name means to him.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time for our independent writing activity. Please sit at the table and start writing your story about what your name means to you.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I dunno what to write. I’m not a good writer, you know?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You just need to concentrate and focus on your work right now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Pretending to be a teacher, using a woman's voice) Don’t make me do the same thing that Ms. Jones did. “Make your story! Make your story!” ((turns the pages)). These are the rules. Don’t tell me you can’t write all the way to the end. Good writers write all the way to the end.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please stop talking and write your sentences down on the paper.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks blankly for several seconds, then runs around the table reaching out to his peers and almost touching them) Got you! You’re it! You can’t get me!

TUTOR: Please stop talking and write your sentences down on the paper.

STUDENT: (Looks blankly for several seconds, then runs around the table reaching out to his peers and almost touching them) Got you! You’re it! You can’t get me!

task.content: Independent writing activity titled 'What my name means to me' following a read-aloud

context.social_setting: Working alongside peers at a table

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: Struggling to start a writing task and expected to produce a written product
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Kept talking to each other, did not write down much, ran around the table recalling his game of tag (reaching out to his peers and almost touching them)
related_quotes: I dunno what to write. I’m not a good writer, you know?
I have a lot of names. People call me Rafael, Rafa, Rafi, Rafito, Muniz … These are all my names.

behavior_patterns.condition: When faced with rigid behavioral and product-oriented rules of regular classroom writing instruction
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Role-playing a teacher to critique the rigid behavioral and product-oriented rules
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Desire to also move beyond school sanctioned writing norms
related_quotes: Don’t make me do the same thing that Ms. Jones [a teacher] did. “Make your story! Make your story!” ((turns the pages)). These are the rules. Don’t tell me you can’t write all the way to the end. Good writers write all the way to the end.
